architecture.mechanism: Gravity-fed serial vial queue with a spring-loaded indexing turntable converts operator hand-loading into a deterministic, single-vial-per-cycle release, eliminating human timing jitter and skipped vials by making each vial's advance mechanically coupled to the previous vial's removal.
architecture.intervention: Replace the manual one-at-a-time loading with a passive, solvent-cleanable, bench-top carousel that holds up to 48 vials in a vertical drop column; a spring-loaded pawl indexes one vial forward per 90° rotation of a hand-cranked or motorized (mains-powered, low-voltage) star wheel, and a microswitch on the mixing chamber door triggers the next vial release only after the previous vial is confirmed seated, with a visible LED countdown per cycle.
architecture.expected_effect: Throughput increases from ~30 to ≥120 samples per day (4×) with start-to-start timing variability reduced from ±5 min (manual) to ±10 s (mechanical), and skipped-vial rate drops from ~1 per 100 to <1 per 1000, measured over a 5-day, 600-sample run.
architecture.falsification_test: Run 200 vials through the device with a high-speed camera and a stopwatch; if the inter-vial release interval shows >20% coefficient of variation or any single vial fails to advance within 2 s of the previous seat confirmation, the mechanism fails.
